summary: The constructive algebra checks out: the formal r-th-root completion, the one-extra-degree strict variant, the quadratic-jet degree bookkeeping, the character-sum acceptance count and the dual-GRS reduction all verify, and every live number I checked (344 witnesses, 108/110, 102->109, 118->124/122, 31/29->31/30, 16 stages, 1934 proposals, 11 moves, 116319 Horner evaluations, IID expectation 102.5 at N127,K39) matches the artifact. The one defect is the tight-degree counterexample (p=5, N=4, K=2, r=2, shifts (0,0,0,1)): it does not state the coset orientation, and the claim holds only for a square common coset. With a non-square common coset (beta=2 or 3) exactly one degree<2 polynomial is a perfect strict solution. The test pins orientation 0, but the note text does not. This is a missing condition in a calibration example, not a flaw in the main constructions.

claims.quote: Thus ALL common-coset inputs are solved perfectly whenever
claims.finding: F=W-T/beta has degree rD and leading coefficient lambda^r, so F^(1/r)=R+O(1/X) and F-R^r has degree <= (r-1)D-1 (r is invertible because r | p-1). Q=beta(R^r-F) has degree < (r-1)D <= K, and at the selected points W vanishes and T=t_i, so Q(a_i)-t_i=beta R(a_i)^r. In the artifact the global/common-coset sources meeting K >= (r-1)ceil(N/r) (N127 K77: 64; N31 K16: 16; r3 N63 K46: 42; r4 N32 K24: 24) all score perfect.

claims.quote: Hence K>=b+1 is a uniform sufficient condition for perfect STRICT common-coset completion
claims.step: Strict Nonzero Powers: Constructive Zero Avoidance
claims.finding: (R+c)^r-R^r=sum_{j>=1} binom(r,j)R^(r-j)c^j has leading term r c R^(r-1) of degree exactly b=(r-1)D when c!=0, and the M+1 candidates 0..M are distinct because M<=N<p. The artifact's ten strict controls are all perfect; the root-zero traps use degree exactly b (2,4,6,14 against thresholds 3,5,7,15), so the extra degree is genuinely used.

claims.quote: the one-trial expected score fraction approaches rho+R below the perfect threshold
claims.step: Constructive Classical Power Completion, lower-rate paragraph
claims.finding: Forcing M ~ rK/(r-1) points and accepting each unseen point with probability ~1/r gives rR/(r-1)+(1-rR/(r-1))/r = R+rho. SCL-(rho+R)=2(sqrt(rho R(1-R)(1-rho))-rho R), which is >0 exactly when R+rho<1, so the 'does NOT match' statement is also right. The artifact's IID expectation for N127,K39 global (78 forced, 236348908444403630002/(2^61-1) ~ 102.5) agrees.

claims.quote: Uniform proposals therefore succeed with probability>=1/3
claims.finding: sum_z chi(a+beta z^2)=-chi(beta) for a!=0 gives sum_z chi((a+beta z^2)/beta_i)=-chi(beta/beta_i), so the accepted count is (p-chi(beta/beta_i)+Z)/2 >= (p-1)/2, and (p-1)/(2p) >= 1/3 for p>=3. The degree check also holds: with h=2D-K+1>0, deg(2R0 L) <= 2D-h=K-1 and deg L^2 <= 2(D-h) < K; the M forced constraints survive any R because W vanishes there.

claims.quote: all25 native polynomials fail perfect strict satisfaction
claims.step: Strict Nonzero Powers, tight-degree paragraph (p5,N4,K2,r2, shifts(0,0,0,1))
claims.finding: The note does not give the coset orientation, and the claim depends on it. Exhaustive check over F5 with points 1..4: for beta in {1,4} (square common coset) no degree<2 polynomial is a perfect strict solution, as claimed; for beta in {2,3} (non-square common coset) exactly one of the 25 polynomials is perfect. The test uses orientation 0, but the statement as written needs 'global input with sigma=0 (beta a square)' added to be a counterexample.

claims.quote: For N127,K39 mixed inputs,102/102 improves to109/109
claims.step: Adaptive Root-Value Exchange Is Now Executed
claims.finding: This matches the artifact: K39 mixed repairs go 102->109 and 102->109, K77 mixed go 118->124 and 118->122, all four end NO_SAMPLED_IMPROVEMENT, and over the 16 r=2 repair stages there are 1934 retained proposals, 11 accepted moves and 116319 native Horner evaluations. The bound passes <= N-initial_score+1 follows because every non-final pass gains at least one point.

summary: The construction is correct: Q=Q0+R^2 with F=R^2-nu Z^2 makes A residues squares and B residues nu-multiples of squares, the degree budget K>max(|A|,D) is exact, the inert/split norm criterion and the Cayley rotation algebra verify, and the p=23 all-parameter counterexample reproduces exactly (D0 coefficients (0,4,14,16), roots 0,9,16, G+V_B=D0*X/16, Q=13 strict-perfect). The IID population bound I_p(D)/p^D is properly derived, and the artifact matches the reported numbers (perfect 127/127 after 1 and 15 base factorizations, degrees 69 and 64, D=58 and 64, K39 not applicable). The one defect: the stated 'at least 1/(2N)' corollary fails in the degenerate case N=1 (|B|=1, D=2 gives (1-1/p)/2 < 1/2). It holds for N>=2, so the population conclusion stands, but the statement needs that condition.

claims.quote: The exact sufficient degree condition is K>max(|A|,D).
claims.finding: deg Q0 <= |A|. Because nu is a non-square the leading terms of R^2 and nu Z^2 cannot cancel, so deg R <= D/2 and deg R^2 <= D. On A, Q0=t_i gives Q-t_i=R^2. On B, V_B=0 gives Q-t_i=R^2-F=nu Z^2. The artifact's 'sufficient_RS_dimension' values 70 and 65 equal max(|A|,D)+1 for (69,58) and (64,64).

claims.quote: Thus a monic polynomial is a norm exactly when every odd-degree irreducible has even multiplicity.
claims.finding: An irreducible of degree d over Fp has gcd(d,2) factors over F_(p^2). Inert odd-degree f has norm f^2, and an even-degree f=g*bar(g) is N(g). The norm map on leading coefficients is onto Fp*, so the monic criterion is right, and N(rho H)=rho^2 F/rho^2=F.

claims.quote: Each forbidden R'(a_i)=0 on A or Z'(a_i)=0 on B has a NONZERO quadratic numerator in s
claims.step: Strict Roots Without A Field-Size Search
claims.finding: alpha_s has norm (1-nu s^2)/(1-nu s^2)=1, and the denominator is nonzero because nu is a non-square. The numerators are nu R s^2+2 nu Z s+R and nu Z s^2+2R s+Z, which vanish identically only if R=Z=0 (p odd); that case is excluded because F(a_i)!=0. So there are <=2N bad s, and 2N+1 distinct candidates exist when p>2N.

claims.quote: Thus NONE of the23 parameters is a norm, although OPI itself is easy.
claims.step: Try To Disprove The Pencil, Then Repair It
claims.finding: Recomputed over F23: V_A-V_B=(0,4,14,16) with roots {0,9,16}; interpolating t_B and adding V_B gives exactly D0*X/16, so F_lambda=D0*(X/16-lambda), whose moving root 16*lambda can pair with at most one fixed root. Q=13 gives 13 (a square) on A and 17,14,5,7 (non-squares) on B, so it is strict-perfect. This matches the artifact's D_coefficients and F_base_coefficients, and the expanded repair succeeds after 5 base factorizations.

claims.quote: Therefore first-trial success is at least I_p(D)/p^D
claims.finding: Given A shifts, lambda and rho, the D values that determine F0 are IID uniform, so F/rho^2=F0/rho^2+V_B is uniform monic of degree D. An irreducible of even degree D>=2 splits over F_(p^2) and has no Fp root, so strict avoidance applies when p>2N. The artifact records the exact bound for D=58 and D=64 on the K77 rows, with strict_zero_avoidance_covered true only on the strict rows; the 127/127 witnesses in 1 and 15 trials also match.

claims.quote: For p>2N the elementary irreducible-count bound gives at least1/(2N).
claims.step: A Rigorous One-Trial Average-Case Statement, corollary
claims.finding: Missing condition N>=2 (and no derivation is shown). Counterexample: N=1 with the single position in B gives D=2, and I_p(2)/p^2=(1-1/p)/2 < 1/2=1/(2N) for every p>2. For N>=2, D <= N+1 <= 2N and (1-2p^(-D/2))/D >= 1/(2N) does hold, so the population conclusion survives.

summary: The load-bearing chain holds: the average uniform-sign TV <= sum_F m_i hybrid bound (derived in the companion note and rechecked), the exact plus/minus posterior-magnitude recursion, its identification with BPQM pure-state combinations (so m_i is a mean overlap, i.e. a root fidelity), and the degradation argument making mesh-rounded-up overlaps and dyadic-rounded-down herald masses valid upper bounds. Every reported number I checked matches the artifacts: the coarse table (16, 78, 361, 1614 at TV <= 0.1, with all half-rate targets uncertified), the 3/8-rate follow-up TV ~ 0.0234307, and the N32768 bound 0.0102208 with 65534 channel combinations and 1,008,335,816 support-pair visits. Rerunning the rounding by hand for N=16 index 0 reproduces the stored 1/256 upper bound. One small provenance point: the N1024, 361-constraint Gibbs sample is executed in the test suite, not stored in the artifact, though the text does not claim otherwise. The scope limits (average sign only, no fixed-grid asymptotics, numerical duality checks only for small N) are stated.

claims.quote: The preceding hybrid argument gives average uniform-sign Gibbs TV at most 2 epsilon_F = sum_F m_i.
claims.finding: With Qjoint having a uniform F-marginal, TV(P_U,Qjoint) <= sum_F E|P(U_i=1|U_<i)-1/2| = (1/2) sum_F m_i, and E_uniform s TV <= TV(Qjoint,P_U)+TV(P_U_F,Unif) <= 2 epsilon_F. Uniform signs J give a uniform syndrome G(J)_F, and y=J+E is a bijection, so the bound transfers to the Gibbs law. The artifact's TV upper is exactly twice 'frozen_prefix_bias_sum_upper', which is consistent.

claims.quote: The odd source bit has magnitudes (a+b)/(1+ab) and |a-b|/(1-ab), with branch weights (1+ab)/2 and (1-ab)/2.
claims.finding: Given U1=X1 xor X2=0, the posterior bias of X2 is [(1+a)(1+b)-(1-a)(1-b)]/[(1+a)(1+b)+(1-a)(1-b)]=(a+b)/(1+ab), with probability (1+ab)/2. Given U1=1 it is |a-b|/(1-ab), and the XOR bit has bias ab. Verified algebraically.

claims.quote: In particular m_i equals the UNSQUARED root Uhlmann fidelity of the reversed synthesized CQ bit-channel.
claims.finding: The base case PSC overlap c equals source bias 1-2p=c. Variable/check combinations of PSCs give overlap ab and heralded {(a+b)/(1+ab), |a-b|/(1-ab)}, and the root fidelity of a heralded pure-state mixture is the weighted mean overlap, so induction gives the identity with indices reversed. The companion artifact's N2 control shows root fidelities [0.65,0.4225] against source mean biases [0.4225,0.65].

claims.quote: The computed mean overlaps are therefore upper bounds on the true m_i.
claims.step: Certified Finite Construction / physical PSC degradation
claims.finding: |psi_x(a)> -> |psi_x(d)> (x) |psi_x(a/d)> preserves the Gram matrix (overlap d*(a/d)=a), so PSC(a) degrades to PSC(d) for a <= d. Moving herald mass to overlap one is a degrading channel, polar combinations of degraded copies are degraded, and fidelity is monotone under CPTP maps. Recomputing the mesh rounding for N=16 index 0 (0.65 -> ... -> 1/256) reproduces the artifact's stored upper bound.

claims.quote: The larger G=256,r=3,b=96 calculation succeeds at N32768, |F|=16384
claims.finding: The parameter-labelled artifact shows TV upper 424553765284920852120940002337825/41538374868278621028243970633760768 ~ 0.0102208 < 0.010221, target_certified true, 65534 (=2^16-2) channel combinations and 1008335816 support-pair visits. The coarse table entries (16, 78, 361, 1614 at TV <= 0.1; half-rate uncertified) and the 3/8 follow-up (1536 constraints, TV 0.0234307) also match.

claims.quote: any polar Gibbs proposal whose justification is a vanishing SUM OF THESE ROOT FIDELITIES also supplies this polynomial classical average-sign sampler
claims.finding: Given the public F, the SC sampler's average-sign TV is bounded by the same sum of root fidelities, and it uses O(N^2) exact rational operations with polynomial bit lengths (they roughly double per level, so O(N) times the input precision). The note limits this to that criterion and the uniform-sign model, and says it does not cover joint receivers or other error criteria.

summary: The Gibbs mapping, the prefix and fair-source exactness, and the hybrid average-syndrome bound (TV(P_U,Qjoint) <= epsilon_F, delta <= epsilon_F, both averages <= 2 epsilon_F) are all correct. The Pinsker/Jensen entropy bound and the reversed-index CQ/source duality follow from the dephasing argument given. I recomputed the whole calibration table exactly (0.4/0.72; 0/0; 0/0; 0.00416611/0.05596208), including the choice {0,1,2,4} as the four smallest exact biases, and the N=2 per-syndrome values (2/25, 18/25, native average 18/125, bound 4/5) match the artifact. The note keeps the worst-sign and asymptotic-construction limits explicit.

claims.quote: Given arbitrary public clause signs J, set s=H_F J and y=E xor J.
claims.finding: H_F y=U_F+H_F J=s+s=0, and Pr(y) is the product of (1-p)=(1+c)/2 when y_j=J_j and p=(1-c)/2 otherwise, which is the stated product of (1+c(-1)^(y_j+J_j)) up to normalisation.

claims.quote: For a contiguous initial frozen prefix, however, the remaining chain is already conditioned on every constraint
claims.finding: When F={0..k-1}, the chain rule P(u|u_F=s)=prod_{i>=k} P(u_i|u_<i) is exact, and for p=1/2 the U_i are IID fair bits. Recomputation gives TV exactly 0 for the N4 {0,1} and N8 {0,1,2} rows.

claims.quote: Thus TV(P_U,Qjoint)<=epsilon_F.
claims.finding: This is a hybrid over frozen indices with per-step cost E|P(U_i=1|prefix)-1/2|. Qjoint's F-marginal is uniform (sum out free coordinates from the last one), so delta <= TV(P_U,Qjoint), and both triangle bounds follow. Exact recomputation: N2 F={1} p=1/10 gives epsilon=2/5, per-syndrome TV 2/25 and 18/25, uniform average 2/5, native average 18/125, and N8 {0,1,2,4} gives 0.004166113/0.055962076, all matching the table and artifact.

claims.quote: Uniform clause signs give uniform syndromes because H_F has full row rank
claims.finding: The rows of H_F are distinct rows of the invertible polar matrix, so they are linearly independent, and a full-rank linear image of a uniform vector is uniform.

claims.quote: Pinsker and Jensen give E|P(U_i=1|prefix)-1/2| <= sqrt((ln 2)/2 * (1-H(U_i|U_<i)))
claims.finding: KL(Bern(q)||Bern(1/2)) = ln2 (1-h2(q)) in nats, so Pinsker gives |q-1/2| <= sqrt(ln2/2 (1-h2(q))), and concavity of sqrt plus E[h2]=H(U_i|U_<i) gives the averaged form.

claims.quote: Hence the CQ information at i equals the source conditional entropy at N-1-i.
claims.step: Why This Is Relevant To The Quantum Proposal
claims.finding: Averaging Z^(uG) over the span of rows >=i dephases |psi_0>^N into blocks whose masses are the Bernoulli(p)^N laws of those row parities. So the CQ Holevo information at i is H(row_i.E | rows>i), and G^T=RGR with RE IID turns this into H(U_(N-1-i)|U_<(N-1-i)). The artifact shows the reversal numerically ([0.4709,0.8671] against [0.8671,0.4709]).
